member.summary: ADR-0192: classifies how a G# partial func projects into the stub. gsc keeps a lone declaring part after GS0609 precisely so a generator can see it and supply the implementation, and C# generators (the Regex generator first among them) only fill in a method declared partial with no body — any other shape is SYSLIB1043 — so that part renders as a C# partial method definition. A pair gsc has already merged renders as a C# definition plus implementation. Every other shape keeps the ordinary-method rendering: a lone implementing part, or the declaring part gsc kept to recover from several declaring parts (both GS0610), a partial method in a non-partial type (GS0608), or a receiver-clause or explicit-interface partial (GS0607). C# would reject a partial member in each of those, and gsc has already reported the real error.

member.name: M:GSharp.GeneratorHost.GsStubRenderer.PlanRecords(System.Collections.Immutable.ImmutableArray{GSharp.Core.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.StructSymbol})
member.summary: Decides which data types render as C# records, across the inheritance graph rather than per type. A C# record derives only from object or another record (CS8864), and only a record derives from a record (CS8865), while a G# data class may derive from any open class and any open class may derive from a data class. So a data type renders as a record only when its base class is a record-rendered data type (or it has none) and every source class deriving from it renders as a record too. Otherwise the whole connected chain stays classes, which is how every data type rendered before (a generator just sees no IsRecord). A base class declared elsewhere (a referenced assembly) is never a record here, so its data descendants stay classes.

member.name: T:GSharp.GeneratorHost.GsStubRenderer
member.summary:
ADR-0145 §B: renders a bound G# global scope into a single declaration-only C# compilation unit ("stub"). The stub carries every user-declared type with its accessibility, base clause, generics/constraints, member signatures, and — critically — every symbol's attributes spelled by fully-qualified CLR metadata name, which is exactly what a Roslyn incremental generator matches on via ForAttributeWithMetadataName. All member bodies are elided (=> throw null!).
The correctness bar is that the emitted text re-parses as valid C#; it is never compiled to a runnable assembly.

member.summary: ADR-0145 §B facade: binds a G# 's global scope and renders the declaration-only C# stub the generator host feeds to Roslyn. Tolerance rule (ADR-0145 §B). This is the reverse of cs2gs's CSharpTypeMapper: cs2gs maps a Roslyn ITypeSymbol onto a canonical G# type; this maps a bound G# back onto a fully-qualified (global::) C# type name.
A type with no faithful C# spelling degrades to the universal upper bound object and the loss is recorded on so the caller can surface a GS9204 info (ADR-0145 §H). The stub only has to re-parse, so the fallback never breaks the pipeline.

Each instance also carries the MSBuild item metadata (build_metadata.AdditionalFiles.*) the generator's lookup needs — most importantly SourceItemGroup (e.g. AvaloniaXaml), which is how such a generator recognizes a file as its own input.

member.name: T:GSharp.GeneratorHost.ImplementingPartHeaders
member.summary:
ADR-0192 follow-on 2, step 4: spells each generated G# implementing part with its user declaring part's own header.
gsc pairs the two parts textually (GS0611 compares normalized header text, and the grouping key compares parameter-type text), but the implementing part is back-translated from the generator's C#, so it spells the header the way cs2gs spells that C# — Regex and int32 — while the user may have written System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex or int. So the implementing part's header (every modifier through the return type, method-level annotations excluded: gsc unions those, and each part keeps its own) is replaced with the declaring part's header text, found through the G# syntax tree of the printed .g.gs and of the user's file. The body is kept.
The copied header must bind in the .g.gs, so the user file's imports are added to it: every namespace import it lacks, and every alias import the copied header names. An alias the .g.gs already binds to a different target is a genuine clash; the header is then left as generated and GS9208 is reported. So is a parameter-name mismatch: the body refers to the parameters by the generated names, which a generator takes from the definition the stub rendered from the user's declaring part, so they normally agree; copying a header whose names differ would rebind the body to different parameters.

member.name: T:GSharp.GeneratorHost.StubDataType
